fixes.regressionTestEvidence: The test asserts consistent=true when edge=core4, exchange=candidate_exchange and closed_loop=core4, and consistent=false when closed_loop is a stale core4 checksum. Reverting the fix makes the test fail; restoring it makes the test pass.
fixes.resolution: Compare snapshot.closed_loop.pool_scope_checksum against snapshot.candidate_edge.pool_scope_checksum, which is also core4 scoped. This matches the documented contract in closed_loop_manager::closed_loop_pool_scope_checksum.
fixes.rootCause: assess_upstream() compared snapshot.closed_loop.pool_scope_checksum with snapshot.candidate_exchange.pool_scope_checksum. closed_loop belongs to the core4 scope (filter_mode edge_any, checksum sha256:335f0bbf05c03ec6a3d780d6e4b462abf3fdcff992baea98d8332c7349c041e9) while candidate_exchange belongs to a different scope (filter_mode both_end, checksum sha256:aae839c344abc67c73ab387147a6d715bd2703db57a7e13426509f5b6c34f5dc). The two can never be equal, so every assessment raised a permanent false positive and CompositeError::UpstreamInconsistent blocked the entire pipeline refresh.
fixes.title: composite_manager compared closed_loop pool scope checksum against the candidate_exchange scope

fixes.resolution: Dry-run then apply POST /v1/closed-loops/rebuild on the testnet database: changedRows=0, consumersNeedRebuild=false, closedLoopVersion=2, checksum unchanged. This is a data-state convergence on the testnet database only; no production write was performed.
fixes.rootCause: consumersNeedRebuild is a sticky transient flag: materialize sets checksum_changed and only a subsequent no-change idempotent materialize clears it. The flag remained set from an earlier materialize, so the assessment still reported closed_loop.consumersNeedRebuild even though the underlying data was already consistent.
fixes.title: Stale consumersNeedRebuild flag blocked the pipeline consistency verdict

summary.failureSetComparisonMethod: Set comparison of the sorted FAILED node-id lists. The round 18 baseline log is UTF-16LE (PowerShell redirect output) and must be decoded as utf-16-le before parsing. The round 18 evidence recorded two different hashes under two different normalisation schemes: b8d8918051c037cb3c9bd6a2ca33a21f6f874d9a068c76a8d963499541a20c98 is sha256 of the newline-joined sorted 97-id baseline set, while da1e23e02485fb78c790064eeca1fb446ba257a76fa8b9ffa563a3f18d73521a was produced by a different normalisation that is not reproducible from the raw id list. The authoritative conclusion for round 19 is therefore the set comparison (0 new / 4 fixed), not the hash comparison.
